subject: microbiology
title: Antigen-Antibody Reactions I: Precipitation, Agglutination, Coombs, Widal and ELISA

steps.tx: **Precipitation** occurs when soluble antigen and antibody form visible lattice at equivalence, read as lines in gel (double immunodiffusion Ouchterlony), arcs under electric fields (immunoelectrophoresis), rings in tubes, or turbidity measured by nephelometry; antigen or antibody excess dissolves lattice (prozone, postzone) so curves, not single points, define it.
steps.say: Soluble antigen plus antibody precipitates at equivalence; excess on either side hides the lattice.

steps.tx: **Precipitation** is a visible lattice of soluble antigen and antibody, stable only near equivalence. On an Ouchterlony plate the lattice is a line in gel, and a continuous arc of identity means two wells share the epitopes recognised. Immunoelectrophoresis bends that line into arcs. Tube rings and nephelometry read the same event as a band or as turbidity. Antigen excess, the postzone, or antibody excess, the prozone, dissolves the lattice, so one dilution can look falsely negative.
steps.say: Soluble antigen and antibody precipitate only near equivalence, seen as lines on an Ouchterlony plate, arcs after electrophoresis, rings in tubes, or turbidity by nephelometry. A fused line of identity means shared epitopes. Too much antigen or antibody, postzone or prozone, dissolves the lattice and can hide the reaction.

vis.alt: An Ouchterlony plate shows wells of antigen and antibody with precipitin lines, including a smooth line of identity between related antigens.
vis.caption: Precipitin arcs form in gel where soluble antigen and antibody meet at equivalence, and a continuous line marks antigenic identity. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Flocculation** is precipitation's fine cloudy cousin (VDRL for syphilis, where cardiolipin antigen flocculates with reagin antibody), while **agglutination** crosslinks particulate antigen (cells, bacteria, latex beads) into visible clumps, faster and more sensitive, powering Widal, blood grouping and latex antigen tests.
steps.say: Particles clump, solubles precipitate, cardiolipin flocculates: aggregate size names the reaction.

left.title: Agglutination family
points: Direct: bacteria and red cells (grouping, Widal)
Passive: antigen coated latex or red cells
Reverse passive: antibody coated particles detect antigen
Coagglutination: staphylococcal protein A carries antibody

right.title: Reading discipline
points: Prozone false negatives at low dilutions

steps.tx: The **Coombs test** (antiglobulin) finds antibodies that coat without clumping: direct test washes patient red cells and adds anti human globulin to reveal in vivo coating (haemolytic disease of newborn, autoimmune haemolysis, transfusion reactions), indirect test coats donor or reagent cells in vitro to screen sera for unexpected antibodies before transfusion and in pregnancy.
steps.say: Direct Coombs reads cells already coated in the patient; indirect coats them in the tube.

left.title: Direct antiglobulin (DAT)
points: Positive: HDN, AIHA, drug and transfusion causes

right.title: Indirect (IAT)
points: Serum plus reagent cells, then AHG

steps.tx: The **Widal test** agglutinates Salmonella Typhi O and H and paratyphi antigens with patient serum, weakened by endemic background titres, prior vaccination, cross reactions and early antibiotics, needing rising paired titres and local cut offs to mean anything. Blood culture in week one outranks it, which the Salmonella module makes the hierarchy to state aloud.
steps.say: A single Widal titre in an endemic town is gossip; paired rising titres approach evidence.

left.title: Widal reading
points: O rises early, falls months; H persists (vaccination confounds)
Local significant titre (often 1:160 and above endemic adjusted)
Paired sera four fold rise stronger
Anamnestic H rises in unrelated fevers

right.title: Typhoid test hierarchy
points: Stool and urine cultures later weeks
Widal and rapid tests supportive only

steps.tx: The **Weil Felix test** exploits cross reacting Proteus antigens (OX19, OX2, OXK) agglutinating with rickettsial antibodies (shared epitopes), a heterophile economy now largely replaced by specific serology and PCR yet immortal in examinations. It teaches that agglutination specificity is epitope luck.
steps.say: Proteus stands in for rickettsiae by shared epitopes; specificity was borrowed, not owned.

left.title: Weil Felix pairings
points: OX19: typhus and Rocky Mountain groups

right.title: Modern successors
points: Weil Felix persists where resources thin

steps.tx: **Complement fixation** (historical Wassermann for syphilis, viral serology era) consumed complement by antigen antibody complexes, reporting haemolysis absence as positive via indicator sheep cells, elegant and now museum grade beside ELISA. Its logic (complement consumed equals antibody present) still explains complement consumption reasoning.
steps.say: No haemolysis meant positive: complement fixation read absence as evidence.

left.title: CF mechanics
points: Test system consumes complement if antibody present
Sensitised sheep red cells as indicator

right.title: CF legacy
points: Complement consumption logic survives in C3 C4 reading

steps.tx: **ELISA** (enzyme linked immunosorbent assay) binds antigen or antibody to plates, detects with enzyme conjugated reagents and coloured substrate, in direct, indirect, sandwich and competitive architectures, quantified against standards. HIV fourth generation (antigen plus antibody), hepatitis serology and dengue NS1 all live on this chassis with chemiluminescence as its luminous upgrade.
steps.say: Sandwich catches antigen, indirect catches antibody; the enzyme's colour is the report.

left.title: ELISA architectures
points: Direct and indirect antigen antibody detection
Cut offs and grey zones require confirms

right.title: ELISA discipline
points: Hook effect at extreme antigen excess
Point of care lateral flow is its paper cousin

steps.tx: **ELISA** fixes antigen or antibody to a plastic well, then detects the partner with an enzyme conjugate and a substrate that becomes coloured. Direct, indirect, sandwich, and competitive layouts answer different questions, and standards turn colour into a quantity. A sandwich layout captures antigen between two antibodies. An indirect layout looks for antibody in the sample. Fourth generation HIV assays combine antigen and antibody on this chassis. Hepatitis serology and dengue NS1 use it as well. Chemiluminescence is the brighter descendant of the same well and enzyme idea.
steps.say: ELISA coats a well with antigen or antibody, adds an enzyme linked partner, and reads coloured substrate against standards. Sandwich assays capture antigen. Indirect assays look for antibody. Competitive and direct layouts are the other architectures. HIV antigen plus antibody tests, hepatitis serology, and dengue NS1 sit on this platform, with chemiluminescence as a brighter version.

vis.alt: A microplate shows wells developing colour after an enzyme linked assay, with standards and samples of different intensity.
vis.caption: Enzyme conjugate turns substrate into colour in wells where antigen or antibody has been captured, and intensity is read against standards. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Serological test evaluation** (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values shifting with prevalence, likelihood ratios, window periods) governs every reaction in this lesson: a 99 percent specific test at 0.1 percent prevalence yields mostly false positives, which is why confirmatory cascades and testing strategies (NACO HIV algorithms) exist instead of single heroic tests.
steps.say: Prevalence writes predictive value; confirmatory cascades exist because arithmetic demands them.
